title: Bypass general ALU for memory addresses
motivation: The current worst path starts at the MEM/WB destination register and passes through forwarding and the EX ALU before reaching the data-memory address. Load/store addresses only need rs1 plus the immediate, but currently share the ALU result path with all other operations, including combinational division.

hypothesis.motivation: The current worst path starts at the MEM/WB destination register and passes through forwarding and the EX ALU before reaching the data-memory address. Load/store addresses only need rs1 plus the immediate, but currently share the ALU result path with all other operations, including combinational division.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a dedicated effective-address result for loads and stores, captured alongside the EX/MEM payload and used directly by the memory stage for address, alignment, and lane selection. Keep the general ALU result for other operations. This removes the ALU operation-selection and M-extension result muxes from the timed memory-address path, which should raise Fmax on CoreMark's frequent memory accesses.

title: Share DIV and REM in an iterative execution unit
motivation: The baseline's worst path crosses forwarding, EX, and the ALU, while the ALU describes four combinational divide/remainder operations. These operators are much deeper than the common integer datapath and can dominate both Tang Nano timing and LUT use, even though CoreMark uses them infrequently.

hypothesis.motivation: The baseline's worst path crosses forwarding, EX, and the ALU, while the ALU describes four combinational divide/remainder operations. These operators are much deeper than the common integer datapath and can dominate both Tang Nano timing and LUT use, even though CoreMark uses them infrequently.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Replace the combinational DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU operators with one shared 32-step iterative divider that captures signedness and quotient-versus-remainder mode, while keeping ordinary integer and multiply operations on the existing single-cycle path. Stall fetch/decode behind an active divide and inject bubbles through EX/MEM while older instructions drain; retire the divide only when its result is ready. This should remove the divider from the EX combinational critical path and share hardware across all four operations, raising Fmax enough to offset the occasional divide latency.

Add divide-busy pipeline control that freezes younger work while allowing older stages to drain without duplicate retirement or memory requests.

title: Static backward-taken branch prediction
motivation: Taken loop branches currently redirect from EX, flushing the two younger instructions on every iteration. CoreMark has many short loops whose conditional branches target lower addresses, so predicting those branches in fetch can avoid recurring pipeline bubbles.

hypothesis.motivation: Taken loop branches currently redirect from EX, flushing the two younger instructions on every iteration. CoreMark has many short loops whose conditional branches target lower addresses, so predicting those branches in fetch can avoid recurring pipeline bubbles.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a static direct-control-flow predictor in IF: predict JAL as taken and conditional branches as taken when their immediate is negative, with all other instructions predicted to continue at PC+4. Carry the predicted next PC through ID/EX and let EX redirect and flush only when its resolved next PC differs, retaining the current trap behavior for misaligned targets. This avoids the two-cycle redirect penalty on common backward loop branches without a predictor table.

title: One-hot register-file read ports
motivation: The improved divider moved the critical path to register-file read and decode, with the path starting at a register bit and reaching the ID/EX operand register. The current variable-index reads and separate write-first bypasses synthesize into muxing on both read ports. CoreMark frequently consumes register operands, so shortening these reads could improve Fmax without adding pipeline latency.

title: Restructure register file read selection
motivation: The current worst path starts in the register file and ends at the ID/EX operand register. The two asynchronous register-file reads use dynamic array indexing, which can map to deep 32-to-1 mux trees on the Tang Nano fabric. The prior structural divider change exposed this register-read path as the new timing limit.

title: Tiny tagged branch target predictor
motivation: Static prediction previously added instruction decode and immediate reconstruction to the fetch-PC path, and regressed timing. Recurrent CoreMark loops still pay redirect bubbles, so a predictor that learns their targets and outcomes without inspecting the fetched instruction may recover those cycles with less fetch logic.

hypothesis.motivation: Static prediction previously added instruction decode and immediate reconstruction to the fetch-PC path, and regressed timing. Recurrent CoreMark loops still pay redirect bubbles, so a predictor that learns their targets and outcomes without inspecting the fetched instruction may recover those cycles with less fetch logic.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add an eight-entry direct-mapped branch target buffer with partial PC tags and two-bit direction counters. Fetch uses only the current PC to look up a previously resolved branch or jump; a hit predicted taken selects the stored target, while misses and predicted-not-taken branches continue at PC+4. EX trains entries only for resolved, non-trapping control instructions, and compares every instruction's architectural next PC against its carried prediction so cold misses and tag aliases are corrected. Existing misaligned-target traps still suppress redirects and predictor training. This removes opcode decode and immediate generation from the fetch prediction path, while repeated loop branches can avoid their recurring redirect bubbles.

title: Bank register-file read muxes
motivation: After removing combinational division, the critical path runs from register-file state through forwarding and pipeline control to an ID/EX operand register. The previous one-hot read implementation increased LUT and FF use, so the read selection should be reorganized while retaining binary muxing and the existing storage and bypass behavior.

hypothesis.hypothesis: Split each asynchronous register-file read into four 8-register banks: select within each bank using the low address bits, then select one bank using the high address bits. This grouped binary mux should localize address fanout and map into the FPGA's small LUTs more efficiently than a flat 32-entry read, shortening the register-file-to-ID/EX path without the wide masked-OR trees of the prior attempt. Preserve x0 behavior, the synchronous write port, and same-cycle write-first bypass semantics.

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes

## Change

Updated `cores/bench/rtl/reg_file.sv` so both asynchronous read ports first
select one of eight registers in each of four banks using address bits `[2:0]`,
then select the bank using address bits `[4:3]`. The 32 x 32 storage array,
synchronous write port, x0 behavior, and same-cycle write-first bypass are
unchanged. No deviations from the hypothesis were needed.

## Validation

- `make lint TARGET=bench`: passed with no warnings.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench bash formal/run_all.sh`: passed,
  53 checks and 0 failures. `make formal TARGET=bench` selects the dual-channel
  wrapper explicitly, which does not match this core's `nret: 1`; the
  auto-detecting command above selects the single-channel wrapper.
- `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: passed for both ELF programs. The default
  `make cosim` prerequisite builds with `NRET=2`; setting `NRET=1` matches this
  core's RVFI ports.
- `make timing TARGET=bench`: place option 0 reported 46.847 MHz and 19 logic
  levels. The worst path starts at register-file state and passes through ID,
  EX, IF, and hazard logic before returning to pipeline state.

## Concerns

The measured timing path still begins at register-file state, and this single
placement option reports 46.847 MHz. The change preserves behavior and passes
formal and cosim, but the local timing result alone does not show a frequency
gain.
lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-001-r3s0 (regression, -0.89%): Banking asynchronous reads into groups of eight kept binary muxing but left the 19-level critical path running from register-file state through pipeline and hazard logic, so mux regrouping alone did not improve this core’s timing.

title: Register control-flow redirects
motivation: The divider change raised Fmax and exposed a long register-file-to-fetch-control path through forwarding, EX branch resolution, IF, hazard logic, and ID. A branch decision currently drives the fetch PC and pipeline flush controls in the same cycle, coupling operand selection to PC update timing.

hypothesis.motivation: The divider change raised Fmax and exposed a long register-file-to-fetch-control path through forwarding, EX branch resolution, IF, hazard logic, and ID. A branch decision currently drives the fetch PC and pipeline flush controls in the same cycle, coupling operand selection to PC update timing.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Capture each resolved, non-trapping branch or jump target in the existing EX/MEM boundary and apply the PC redirect in the following cycle. Keep an immediate EX squash signal to bubble the younger instruction as soon as the decision is known, and squash again while the registered target is applied so no sequential-path instruction can retire. This adds one bubble to taken control flow but removes the EX target-to-PC path from the long register-file feedback path; the resulting Fmax increase should outweigh the modest CoreMark cycle cost.

title: Single-entry backward loop predictor
motivation: Prior IF-side static prediction added instruction decode and target arithmetic to the fetch path, while an eight-entry BTB added lookup and target selection delay. CoreMark repeats backward loop branches, so a single exact-match entry may capture the active loop with less lookup logic and avoid most taken-loop redirects.

hypothesis.motivation: Prior IF-side static prediction added instruction decode and target arithmetic to the fetch path, while an eight-entry BTB added lookup and target selection delay. CoreMark repeats backward loop branches, so a single exact-match entry may capture the active loop with less lookup logic and avoid most taken-loop redirects.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a one-entry backward-branch predictor holding a full branch-PC tag, target, and two-bit saturating direction counter. IF predicts the stored target only on an exact PC match with a taken counter; all other fetches use PC+4, without decoding imem_data or reconstructing immediates. EX trains the entry only for backward conditional branches and compares the resolved next PC with the carried prediction, redirecting on a mismatch. The single tag comparison and target mux should cost less timing and area than the prior BTB while repeated CoreMark loops amortize their redirect bubbles.
